Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an AI agent pane: a React/TypeScript page under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/` inside a wxWebView, with the host bridge under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Read `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, and "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` first; every colour, size and radius comes from the token file through the CSS variables, and the design source of truth is the "JusPrin v2" canvas artifact named in that doc. On 2026-10-28 a UX walkthrough of the built app (jusprin-newui, Claude Opus 5.5) found that after the person sent "Is it still fine to print like this?" the chat pane stayed scrolled on the earlier plan message; the question and the agent's answer were below the fold and took a long scroll to reach. Seen once. The critique with screenshots is at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR, frames 2C-04 (stuck view) and 2C-05 (the answer after scrolling). Kenneth wants this task to also tighten the pane's scrolling experience: how the pane indicates there is more below the fold, and how the person jumps straight to the most recent turn. He decides the design; bring him the choices before implementing. Rules: temp docs untracked, never committed; the web bundle is rebuilt through CMake after page changes; page tests are Vitest under `AgentUI`; guard tests must be shown to fail first when they guard a rule; do not commit unless Kenneth asks; several sessions build on this Mac, so check `pgrep -fl ninja` and build with `-j4`. Reproduction routes: the real app (copy the built .app out of the worktree's `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` and `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch folder, set `local_machines` to `{}` in the copied conf, launch with `--datadir <scratch>`, open `~/Downloads/general_purpose_hook.STL`, give a purpose, wait for the plan, then type a question; the web view needs full-screen computer control, which Kenneth approves per request), or the page alone in the built-in browser by injecting a fake `window.wx` host into the built bundle and replaying a long conversation, which needs no screen control.

Task:
Problem: the Agent pane did not scroll to a newly sent message and its answer. After the person typed a question under a long plan message, the pane stayed where it was; the question and the reply were below the fold with no sign they existed, and reaching them took a long scroll. Frames 2C-04 and 2C-05 of the critique show it. It was seen once, so it may depend on scroll position, on streaming, or on the pane's height.

Task, in this order:
1. Reproduce it. Find the pane's scroll logic in the page (`MessageList` and whatever owns auto-scroll on new messages and during streaming) and establish exactly when auto-scroll is skipped: the person had scrolled up to read the plan, so the usual "stick to bottom only when already at bottom" rule is a likely cause. Confirm whether the pane also fails to follow a streaming answer, an app-started turn (a slice ending), and the person's own sent message, since those are three different triggers.
2. Write an untracked note (`chat-scroll-options.md` in the worktree root) proposing the behaviour, for Kenneth to decide. Cover at least: when the pane follows new content and when it holds still (the person's own send should always bring their message into view; an answer arriving while they are reading above should not yank them); how the pane shows there is more below the fold (a "new reply" pill, a count, a shadow at the bottom edge, or the composer's own state); and a jump-to-latest control (where it sits, when it appears, what it says). Compare with how the design-system doc already treats pinned elements and the composer. Keep the proposal small and draw the states as boards on the JusPrin v2 canvas only if the note cannot say it in words.
3. Stop and wait for Kenneth's choice. Do not implement before he answers.

Done, after his choice, means: the chosen behaviour implemented in the page with tokens only, no literals; Vitest coverage for the follow and hold rules and for the below-the-fold indicator; verified in the real app or the page fixture with screenshots of a held view with the indicator showing and of the jump landing on the latest turn; nothing committed until Kenneth says so; report what was verified and what was not.

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in the design artifacts, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
- Setup card warnings: a warning is only an annotation of the one line it contradicts, drawn directly under it, one per line: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` beside Body Small text in `text.primary`. The three in use: "Plan needs another look · <the edit's label>" under the plan (the app's mark after an edit that was not the agent's, cleared only by the agent recording the plan again), "Printer last reported <material>" under the presets, and "Previous estimates · not current" with a Recompute link under the estimates. A warning that names no line of the card is not the card's: print issues belong to the canvas and the chat; a mismatch between the selection and the connected machine (its nozzle, its model, what it has loaded) belongs to the chat and to the send dialog, never to the chip (see Header chip). Moments of change ("Updated", the last step with Undo, an estimate before and after, an edit by hand, "Confirmed") are the timeline rows', never the card's.
- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate and warning glyphs sit inside a row of Label text, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.
- All settings panel (the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", the four "All settings" boards): opened from the "All settings" link at the end of the setup card's presets line, it takes the Agent pane's place under a header of the compact icon button back to the chat, the title in Body Bold and the pane's own toggle. A "Showing" row holds the design system's Select (`component.select`: 26 DIP, `small` radius, Body text, a 16 DIP chevron, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that strengthens on hover and becomes the focus ring when open; its menu is the Menu/Popover under its left edge, as wide as the field) listing the whole project, each plate when there are two or more, and each object; it follows the selection in the 3D view. Under it a Field/Search ("Search settings") beside an All / Changed Segmented Control. The presets in use sit in a `surface.subtle` box with the `medium` radius, each filament slot with its Swatch (`component.swatch`, 24 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke). Groups are OrcaSlicer's own pages (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial, Others, then Filament and Printer) with a 32 DIP header row (16 DIP chevron, Body Small Bold name, Label summary at the right) and rows indented 24 DIP: Body Small name and value on a 28 DIP line, a changed value in Body Small Bold with "Preset: …" in Metadata under it. Two or three filament slots stand side by side, one column per slot; more than three go through a slot picker, one at a time. The host reads the whole table in one message (`settings_catalog`, the `all_settings` capability). Only one object's view has anything to press: a Button/Link at the end of a row's note, under the value, where the table marks one — "Use project value" under a setting the object, a part, a modifier or a height range sets itself (not a range's own layer height or filament, which define it), and "Remove" under its support blockers or enforcers. Each press is one OrcaSlicer undo step of the person's, named for what it did, and the panel redraws from the host's next table (`settings_action`, the `settings_actions` capability).
- Shared progress track: 4 DIP from `component.progress.height`; PrinterCard and Agent activity use this role rather than owning separate track heights.
- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
- Icon button: 32×32 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius (`component.button.icon`).
- Compact icon target: 26×26 DIP (`component.button.iconCompact`), only for the canvas tool strip and the reset button in a form row, which stands at the field's height.
- Link button: 26 DIP high, 4 DIP horizontal padding, Label Bold in `action.primary`, underlined on hover (`component.button.link`).
- Segmented control: a 30 DIP `surface.subtle` track with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` border and 2 DIP padding, holding 24 DIP segments in Label; the chosen one is `action.primary` (`component.segmented`).
- Tooltip: 24 DIP high, 4×8 DIP padding, Metadata, inverse (`text.primary` fill, `surface.canvas` text) with the subtle elevation (`component.tooltip`). Native tooltips are the operating system's own.
- Header chip: 28 DIP high, `chip` radius (`component.chip`). The chip states the selection: the printer profile the project will be sliced for, its nozzle, the project's filaments. It may qualify that statement, and must, when the plain statement would mislead; the qualification is about the selection itself, comes from OrcaSlicer's own state, and holds regardless of what the chat says. The chip makes no claim about the physical machine: what is loaded, which plate is on, which nozzle is fitted, whether it is connected or busy. Those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row, and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip. (Kenneth, 2026-09-06, restated 2026-10-28: the September rule "the chip states facts and never warns" was about the chat steering the chip and about mismatches with the connected machine; it was not about the selection.) Four tests for any mark proposed for the chip:
  1. Is it about the selection or about the machine? Machine means not on the chip.
  2. Would the chip's plain text mislead without it? If not, it is a warning, and warnings go to the chat.
  3. Does it come from OrcaSlicer's preset state, or from an observation or a judgement? Observations and judgements go to the chat.
  4. Can the chat create or clear it? If yes, it is not the chip's.

  The one mark in use passes all four. Its printer half is marked while the selected printer profile is not one of the person's named printers and not OrcaSlicer's placeholder (`Printers::printer_from_file`), which is what opening a 3MF saved for another printer leaves selected: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` takes the printer glyph's place, the label reads "<model> · <nozzle> · from the file" in `text.primary`, and the tooltip names the file. The chip's menu then opens with that printer and the Body Small line "From the file · not one of your printers", a row that cannot be pressed; every other row is the stock menu. Nothing is stored: the mark goes when a named printer is selected, from the menu or by the agent. Decided 2026-10-28; boards 1 to 5 of "File for another printer" on the canvas's Printer & Material Settings page.
- Reply choice (Chat/Reply Choice): drawn as a reply the person could send, not as an app control. 28 DIP high with `component.replyChip` padding, the `full` radius (the one capsule control), Body `text.primary` on `surface.subtle` (the person's own bubble) with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke; hover and pressed go to `surface.selected`, never `action.primary`. A tapped choice is sent as the person's bubble in the same tint and words.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the boards on the canvas's Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Agent-pane collapse: an icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

# Agent pane scrolling: what is wrong and three decisions for Kenneth

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28. Branch `claude/chat-scroll` (cut from
origin/jusprin-newui 434e893a6b, nothing changed yet).

## What happened in the walkthrough, and why

The pane follows new content only while the reader is within 24 px of the
bottom. Scrolling up anywhere switches following off, and only scrolling back
down switches it on again (`MessageList.tsx`, `followBottom`). Nothing else
resets it: not the person's own message.

The walkthrough scrolled up to read the plan (frame 1B-06 says "The plan,
scrolled up"). The pane then stayed parked there through the ABS change and
the manual slice (2C-03 shows the same scroll position), so when the question
"Is it still fine to print like this?" was sent, both it and the answer were
added below the fold. Nothing on screen said they existed.

Reproduced in the built page with a fake host (340 × 720 window, 413 px of
thread). Each case below is "where the reader was" → "what the pane did":

| Trigger | At the bottom | Scrolled up |
|---|---|---|
| The person sends a message | follows | **stays put; the message lands 419 px below the view** |
| Same, but only 40 px above the bottom | | **stays put; message 88 px below** |
| Agent answer streaming | follows every word | stays put |
| App-started turn (a slice ends, then the agent reports) | follows | stays put |
| A slice card starts | follows | stays put |

Screenshot of the stuck state:
`/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-napier-147653/e205b652-5d1b-44cc-aa1e-2a1afbfd5940/scratchpad/repro-send-while-held.jpg`

So there are two defects: the person's own message does not override "hold",
and when the pane holds, nothing shows that something new is below.

Found on the way: when the person types several lines, the composer grows and
covers the last 100 px of the thread, even at the bottom, because a change in
the thread's height does not count as new content. Same rule, same fix; I
would fix it in this change unless you say otherwise.

## The design system today

- The pinned setup card already has an edge rule: while the thread is
  scrolled under it, the card gets the `elevation.subtle` shadow below its
  divider. The bottom edge (above the composer) has no matching rule.
- The `full` radius is reserved: the reply choice is "the one capsule
  control". A floating "New reply" pill in capsule form would break that, so
  the options below use the existing 4 DIP button shapes.
- The closest floating control in the app is the canvas's "N print issues"
  button at the canvas's bottom edge.

## Decision 1: what a sent message does

**1A. Jump to the bottom and follow.** Today's behaviour, applied even after
scrolling up. Simple. But a long answer streams past the top of the view, and
the person ends at its last line and has to scroll up to read its start. That
is how the walkthrough came to scroll up in the first place.

**1B. Bring the person's message to the top of the pane, then hold.**
(Recommended.) The answer streams in below the question and the view stops
moving once the turn fills the pane; the reader starts at the top of the
answer. The rest shows through the jump control below. Claude.ai and ChatGPT
work roughly this way.

Either way, "sent" means any new message from the person, so Ask AI from the
issue chip and tapping a reply choice count too. Answers and app-started turns
that arrive while the person is scrolled up never move the view.

## Decision 2: how the pane says there is more below

**2A. A jump button only.** (Recommended.) It appears whenever the bottom of
the thread is out of view. It's a 32 DIP icon button (`button.icon`, Lucide
`arrow-down`) on `surface.canvas`, with a `border.subtle` stroke and
`elevation.subtle`, centred 8 DIP above the composer box. Pressing it is
decision 3.

**2B. 2A, plus a label when something is new.** If a reply or report arrived
while the person was scrolled up, the button becomes "New reply" with the
arrow (`button.secondarySmall`, 28 DIP), and goes back to the plain arrow once
seen. This tells someone reading the plan that the agent has said something.
It costs one more state to test.

**2C. 2A or 2B, plus a shadow above the composer.** This matches the setup
card's top-edge shadow at the bottom edge. It's cheap and consistent. On its
own it is too quiet to say that a new answer arrived.

I would not use a count ("2 new"). A turn can be a message, a slice card and
change rows, so the number would not match what the person sees.

I reproduced the stuck chat and wrote the options note, [chat-scroll-options.md](chat-scroll-options.md), in the worktree root. It's untracked and nothing is implemented. I'm stopping here until Kenneth picks a design.

**Cause.** The pane follows new content only while the reader is within 24 px of the bottom. Scrolling up turns following off, and only scrolling back down turns it on again. A message the person sends doesn't turn it back on. In the walkthrough, frame 1B-06 scrolled up to read the plan, and the pane stayed at that position through 2C-03. So when the question was sent, both it and the answer landed out of view, with nothing on screen to say so.

**Trigger results.** I tested this in the built Agent page with a scripted fake host, in a 340 × 720 window:

| Trigger | At the bottom | Scrolled up |
|---|---|---|
| The person sends a message | follows | stays put; the message lands 419 px below the view |
| Same, starting 40 px above the bottom | — | stays put; the message lands 88 px below |
| An answer streaming in | follows every word | stays put |
| A turn the app starts (a slice ends and the agent reports) | follows | stays put |

So there are two problems: the person's own message doesn't override the hold, and nothing shows that there is more below.

I also found a related problem: typing several lines makes the composer grow, and it covers the last 100 px of the thread even when you're at the bottom. It's the same follow rule, so I'd fix it in the same change.

**The three decisions, with my recommendation:**
- **When you send a message:** bring your message to the top of the pane and hold there while the answer fills in below it. The alternative is to jump to the bottom and follow, which leaves you on the last line of a long answer. That is why the walkthrough had to scroll up to read the plan.
- **Showing there's more below:** a 32 DIP arrow button just above the composer. It says "New reply" when something arrived while you were scrolled up. I'd avoid a pill shape, because the design system reserves the capsule for reply chips. I'd also avoid a count, because a turn can include cards and change rows, so a number wouldn't match what you see. A shadow above the composer, matching the one under the setup card, is optional.
- **Where the jump lands:** at the start of the newest turn if it's taller than the pane, otherwise at the bottom.

This needs no new tokens, only one new icon file (`arrow-down`) next to the existing `arrow-up`.

The fake-host page is still served at `http://localhost:8765/agent.html` from my scratchpad, so I can reuse it to verify the build.

# Agent pane scrolling: what is wrong, what everyone else does, and two decisions

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28, revised after looking at how other AI chat
UIs handle this. Branch `claude/chat-scroll` (cut from origin/jusprin-newui
434e893a6b, nothing changed yet).

## What happened in the walkthrough, and why

The pane follows new content only while the reader is within 24 px of the
bottom. Scrolling up anywhere switches following off, and only scrolling back
down switches it on again (`MessageList.tsx`, `followBottom`). Nothing else
resets it, including the person's own message.

The walkthrough scrolled up to read the plan (frame 1B-06, "The plan,
scrolled up"). The pane then stayed parked through the ABS change and the
manual slice (2C-03 shows the same position), so the question "Is it still
fine to print like this?" and its answer were added below the fold. Nothing
on screen said they existed.

Reproduced in the built page with a fake host (340 × 720 window, 413 px of
thread):

| Trigger | At the bottom | Scrolled up |
|---|---|---|
| The person sends a message | follows | **stays put; the message lands 419 px below the view** |
| Same, from only 40 px above the bottom | | **stays put; message 88 px below** |
| Agent answer streaming | follows every word | stays put |
| App-started turn (a slice ends, the agent reports) | follows | stays put |

Screenshot of the stuck state:
`/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-napier-147653/e205b652-5d1b-44cc-aa1e-2a1afbfd5940/scratchpad/repro-send-while-held.jpg`

Also found: typing several lines grows the composer, which then covers the
last 100 px of the thread even at the bottom, because the thread getting
shorter does not count as a reason to follow.

## What the established chat UIs do

I looked at the chat components that AI products are built from. They all
publish their scroll behaviour, which the products themselves do not:

- **use-stick-to-bottom** (StackBlitz; runs bolt.new, and Vercel's AI
  Elements `Conversation` is built on it): follows the bottom; a scroll up by
  the person releases it; content that grows or shrinks, including a resize,
  never releases it. A round down-arrow button, centred at the bottom of the
  thread, shows whenever the view is not at the bottom and scrolls there.
- **Vercel AI Elements**: `ConversationScrollButton` "appears when the user
  has scrolled up, allowing them to return to the bottom."
- **assistant-ui**: two modes. The default, "bottom", is classic chat that
  scrolls to the bottom when a run starts. "top" places the new user message
  at the top of the viewport and does not follow the answer.
- **Nuxt UI ChatMessages**: a sent message is scrolled to the top of the
  viewport, and the space under it is reserved so it can stay there while the
  reply arrives. Following the stream is off by default. A round, outlined
  `arrow-down` button, centred above the prompt, appears when scrolled up.
- **shadcn Message Scroller**: the sent message moves "near the top", with a
  slice of the previous item still visible above it, and the reply streams
  into the room below. Scrolling away by wheel, touch, keys or the scrollbar
  releases following. Its jump button "brings the reader back and resumes
  following". Its guidance: "Follow only while they're following."
- **ChatGPT**: no first-party description. A feature request from August 2026
  says it follows a long answer to its end, and that the poster has to scroll
  back several screens to find where it started. They ask for exactly the
  "top" behaviour plus a "↓ Jump to latest" button. Users describe a small
  down arrow that appears when scrolled up.

Where they all agree:

1. **Sending always moves the view to the person's message.** Some go to the
   bottom, some put the message at the top, but none leaves it off-screen.
   Ours does; that is the bug.
2. A scroll up by the person stops following. New content never moves a
   reader who has scrolled away.
3. **One plain down-arrow button, centred just above the composer**, shown
   only while the view is not at the bottom. None of them uses a label, a
   count or an edge shadow.
4. The button lands at the bottom and following resumes.
5. Following survives size changes, so the composer growing keeps the bottom
   in view.

## Changes from my first proposal

- Dropped the "New reply" label, the shadow above the composer and the "jump
  to the start of the newest turn" landing. None of the reference designs
  does them. The button is plain and lands at the bottom (points 3 and 4).
- Kept "bring the message to the top" as an option, because three of the five
  components ship it and the ChatGPT request asks for it. It is no longer the
  only answer: "scroll to the bottom and follow" is just as standard.

## Decision 1: where the person's sent message lands

**1A. At the bottom; the answer is followed as it streams.** This is
use-stick-to-bottom, AI Elements and assistant-ui's default, and what ChatGPT
reportedly does. It is the smallest change: it only adds "a new message from
the person scrolls to the bottom and follows" to today's code. The cost is
that a long answer ends on its last line, and the person scrolls up to find
its start. That is what made the walkthrough scroll up to read the plan.

**1B. Near the top, with a peek of the previous item; the answer fills in
below it and the view then holds.** (Recommended.) This is Nuxt UI,
assistant-ui "top" and shadcn, and it is what the ChatGPT request asks for.
The person starts reading their question and the top of the answer; the rest
is one press of the arrow away. It needs room reserved under the last turn
so the message can sit at the top while the answer is still short.

Either way, "sent" means any new message from the person, including Ask AI
from the issue chip and a tapped reply choice. Answers and app-started turns
never move a reader who has scrolled away.

## Decision 2: the jump button's shape

Every reference design uses a **circle**. Our design system reserves the
`full` radius for the reply choice ("the one capsule control"), and its own
icon button is a 32 DIP square with the 4 DIP radius.

**2A. A 32 DIP circle**, `surface.canvas` with a `border.subtle` stroke and
`elevation.subtle`, Lucide `arrow-down`. It matches what people already know,
and needs a sentence in the design-system doc that allows the full radius on
this one icon button. (Recommended.)

**2B. The design system's 32 DIP icon button (4 DIP radius)**, same fill,
stroke, shadow and icon. It needs no doc change, but looks unlike the control
people know from other chat apps.

Either way it is centred 8 DIP above the composer box and floats over the
thread. `arrow-down` gets pinned next to the `arrow-up` already in
`resources/jusprin/ui/icons`. No new tokens are needed.

## How to build it: borrow, don't rewrite

`use-stick-to-bottom` 1.1.6 is MIT, has no dependencies, and supports React
18. It already handles the hard parts: telling the person's scroll from
content growth, resizes (which fixes the composer bug), and keeping the view
still when content above it changes. It has a `targetScrollTop` option for a
scroll target other than the very bottom, which is how 1B would place the
message at the top. I'd recommend adopting it in place of the hand-written
`followBottom` logic, unless you would rather not add a dependency to the
page. In that case the same rules are about 60 lines of our own code.

2. **Scrolling up stops following.** After that, a streaming answer or other new content never moves the reader.
3. **One plain round down-arrow button, centred just above the message box.** It shows only while the view isn't at the bottom. None of them uses a label, a count or an edge shadow.
4. **Pressing it goes to the bottom,** and following starts again.
5. **Following survives size changes.** That also fixes our second problem, where a growing message box covers the end of the thread.

**What I dropped:** the "New reply" label, the shadow above the message box, and landing the jump on the newest turn instead of the bottom.

**Two decisions left for you:**
- **Where a sent message lands.**
  - Scroll to the bottom and follow the answer as it streams. This is use-stick-to-bottom, AI Elements and assistant-ui's default.
  - Or put the message near the top and let the answer fill in below it. This is Nuxt UI, shadcn and assistant-ui's "top" mode. It's also what an August 2026 ChatGPT feature request asks for, because following a long answer leaves you on its last line. That's why the walkthrough had to scroll up to read the plan.
  - I recommend the top placement.
- **The button's shape.** Every reference uses a circle. Our design system reserves the fully round shape for reply choices, and its own icon button has 4 DIP corners. I recommend the circle plus one sentence in the design-system doc allowing it.

**How to build it:** I'd rather adopt `use-stick-to-bottom` than keep our own hand-written follow logic. It's MIT-licensed, has no dependencies and supports our React version. It already handles telling the person's scrolling apart from growing content, and resizes. It also has an option to aim the scroll somewhere other than the very bottom, which the top placement needs. content.text:
I implemented Kenneth's chosen design (scroll to the bottom on send, plus the jump button) on branch `claude/chat-scroll`, uncommitted. The decision reached me through the "Chat: scroll to new answers" session, which quoted Kenneth's approval. A message from the person now always scrolls to the bottom and follows the reply. Scrolling up holds the view, and a jump button shows while the bottom is out of view. All 616 page tests pass, and I checked it in the page with a fake host, not in the built app.

**What changed**
- [MessageList.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx) now uses `use-stick-to-bottom` 1.1.6 in place of the hand-written follow logic.
  - The library only watches the content's height, so I added one resize watch on the thread itself. That keeps the bottom in view when the composer grows.
  - The newest message from the person (typed, reply chip, Ask AI) scrolls to the bottom and turns following back on.
  - With the system's reduced-motion setting on, the scroll jumps instead of easing.
- **Jump button:** 32 DIP, using only existing tokens. It's centred 8 DIP above the composer, has the label "Jump to latest" for screen readers, and pressed and hover states.
- I pinned Lucide `arrow-down.svg` next to `arrow-up.svg` and added it to `lucide-map.json`.
- The thread now has an inner column, `.message-list-content`, which the library watches. I updated three ChangeRows tests and one preview page that looked at the old structure.
- I added one paragraph to [design-system.md](agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md) allowing the full radius on this one button and stating the scroll rules.
- I updated [chat-scroll-options.md](chat-scroll-options.md) (untracked) to record the decision.

**Tests**
- [MessageList.scroll.test.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.scroll.test.tsx) has five tests: following answers and app-started turns at the bottom, holding when scrolled up with the button showing, the person's message pulling the view down, the composer growing, and the jump button.
- I broke each of the four rules in turn and the matching tests failed, then restored the code from a saved copy.
- At first the composer test passed even with its rule removed, because of a leftover animation from opening the thread. I fixed the test so it now catches the break.

**Checked in a real browser (Chromium, 340 × 720)**
- The pane follows an answer and a slice report while at the bottom.
- After a mouse-wheel scroll up, it holds still while a 100-word answer and a slice report arrive, and the button shows.
- The jump lands at the bottom, the button goes away, and following resumes.
- Six lines in the composer keep the bottom in view.
- Sending a question after scrolling up lands at the bottom and follows the reply.

Two screenshots, the held view with the button and the view after the jump, are in `scratchpad/shots/`:
`/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-priceless-napier-147653/e205b652-5d1b-44cc-aa1e-2a1afbfd5940/scratchpad/shots/1-held-with-jump-button.png`

**Not verified**
- **The built app:** this worktree has no native build. I rebuilt the web bundle with the same npm steps the CMake target runs.
- **The C++ token guard tests** (`brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`): they need that build to run.
- **Dark mode:** not checked.

**Open question for Kenneth**
`radius.full` is 14 in both the token file and the canvas, so the "circle" is really a rounded square with 4 DIP of flat side. It matches the decided board exactly; a true circle needs a token change.
